key_insight: Dopamine combines Cartesian-grid large-eddy simulation with free-surface and particle modelling to study small-scale turbulent physics in coastal waves.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports investigation of wave interactions with seabeds, coastal obstacles, and heavy or buoyant particles.
method: Geometric volume-of-fluid wave tracking on a staggered Cartesian grid.
Ghost-cell immersed boundaries for stationary solids and one-way-coupled Lagrangian point particles.
Vreman and anisotropic minimum-dissipation sub-grid-scale turbulence models.
evidence_signal: Analytical, experimental, and numerical comparisons support wave and particle predictions; two-fluid scaling efficiencies reach 77% strong and 73% weak at 512 CPU ranks relative to 64, and a single-GPGPU build was verified against the CPU solver.
watch_item: One-way particle coupling omits particle feedback on the flow, limiting applicability when particle loading materially affects wave or turbulence dynamics.
paper_title: Dopamine: A Cartesian grid large-eddy-simulation framework for coastal ocean modelling of free-surface waves
